# Chapter 3: Arrival

The city came up out of the plain the way a ship comes up out of fog: first a smudge, then a
line, then all at once too large to look at. Mara walked toward it for most of a day.

At the gate a clerk with a ledger asked her name, her business, and the weight of her load.

"Mara. Salt. Eleven hundredweight."

He wrote it down. He did not look up. "You're late," he said, "or early. I can't tell which."

She laughed, and it surprised them both.
